questions.question_text:
What is Debt?(Section 1: What is Debt? Understanding Loans in Family Contexts)
Debt is best defined as:

options.text: Money you save for future goals.
Money you borrow with a promise to repay, often with interest.
Money you earn from a job or allowance.
Money you spend on daily needs like food.Correct Answer: b) Money you borrow with a promise to repay, often with interest.

questions.question_text:
Common Reasons for FamilyLoans(Section 1: What is Debt? Understanding Loans in Family Contexts)
Which of the following is a common reason families might take on debt?

options.text: Buying a new video game console for entertainment.
Taking a luxury vacation abroad.
Paying for a home or car through a loan.
Purchasing daily groceries.Correct Answer: c) Paying for a home or car through a loan.

questions.question_text:
Understanding InterestRates(Section 2: Interest Rates and Borrowing: Education Loans, Personal Loans, and More)
What is an interest rate?

options.text: The total amount of money borrowed.
A fee or percentage charged on borrowed money as the cost of borrowing.
The monthly payment made to repay a loan.
The time period over which a loan is repaid.Correct Answer: b) A fee or percentage charged on borrowed money as the cost of borrowing.

questions.question_text:
Types ofLoans(Section 2: Interest Rates and Borrowing: Education Loans, Personal Loans, and More)
Which type of loan typically has a higher interest rate due to being unsecured and riskier for lenders?

options.text: Education Loan
Home Loan
Personal Loan
Car LoanCorrect Answer: c) Personal Loan

questions.question_text:
Cultural Views onDebt(Section 3: Cultural Perspectives on Debt: Why Avoiding Unnecessary Borrowing Matters)
In many cultural contexts, such as in Indian traditions, debt is often:

options.text: Encouraged for all types of purchases to build wealth.
Seen as a last resort and avoided for non-essential items.
Considered irrelevant to financial planning.
Always viewed as a positive way to achieve goals.Correct Answer: b) Seen as a last resort and avoided for non-essential items.

questions.question_text:
Avoiding UnnecessaryDebt(Section 3: Cultural Perspectives on Debt: Why Avoiding Unnecessary Borrowing Matters)
What is one key reason to avoid unnecessary debt, as discussed in the chapter?

options.text: It helps you spend more on fun activities.
It prevents financial stress and preserves future freedom.
It guarantees a higher credit score instantly.
It ensures you can borrow more in the future.Correct Answer: b) It prevents financial stress and preserves future freedom.
